summary: Extends the Sieve vacation extension with a :seconds parameter, which allows auto-replies to the same sender more than once in a single day. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This Sieve extension adds :seconds to set how long to wait before replying to the same sender again. It allows intervals shorter than a day, including zero when every message should receive a reply.

questions: what is the sieve vacation seconds parameter
what does seconds zero mean in sieve vacation
can a sieve vacation action use days and seconds
subtitle: A Sieve vacation parameter for setting the auto-reply interval in seconds.

tldr.problem: The Vacation extension's days parameter cannot express intervals shorter than a day.
tldr.mechanism: The :seconds parameter sets the minimum time between replies to the same sender and is used instead of :days.
tldr.outcome: A value of zero means reply to every message; implementations may limit high reply rates.

today: RFC 6131 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: More Precise Vacation Intervals
sections.content:
The Sieve Vacation extension generates automatic replies and uses :days to limit replies to the same sender. Some situations need a finer interval than a whole number of days.

This RFC adds :seconds for that purpose.
sections.plainLanguage: The original Vacation extension measures its reply interval in days. This addition lets a script set the interval in seconds.

sections.title: The :seconds Parameter
sections.content:
:seconds sets the minimum interval in seconds between consecutive replies to a sender. If present, it is used instead of :days; using both parameters in one vacation action MUST cause a Sieve processing error.

Values must be at least 0 and less than 2**31, and all valid values MUST be accepted. The capability vacation-seconds implies vacation.
sections.plainLanguage: A vacation action uses either days or seconds, not both. The seconds value sets the minimum wait between replies to one sender.

sections.title: Site Limits, Zero, and Security
sections.content:
A site MAY set minimum and maximum effective values. A maximum effective value MUST be at least 86400 seconds. If the script uses :seconds 0, the system sends every auto-reply and does not suppress consecutive replies.

The RFC says implementations SHOULD consider how many messages small intervals could generate and MAY impose limits. It registers the vacation-seconds capability.
sections.plainLanguage: Zero means reply to every message. Sites may set limits because very short waits can produce many automatic replies.
